dedupe_keys.name: food defence exercise agent based simulation of a bioterrorist attack on the food supply chain

description: This case study describes an agent-based simulation built to train and analyse decisions during a deliberate contamination attack on the food supply chain. The authors, at Purdue University, fed the simulation with production information, consumption patterns, illness and death rates and recall costs, and ran an exercise in which forty food industry representatives made recall and testing decisions based on test results, press releases, epidemiological data and discussions with other industry and regulatory teams; the work is published in a journal article whose free copy, available online as a PDF, is marked public domain. Coverage is a representative United States food supply scenario. Caveats: the attack is hypothetical, the model's detailed parameters are not all published, and outcomes depend on the participants in one exercise. The decisions taken led to over 76,000 illnesses, 45 deaths and 132 million dollars in recall costs, compared with 91,000 illnesses and 54 deaths without intervention. Participants learned that communication between groups is essential and hard, that food safety approaches do not transfer to food defence, and that hiring procedures need more security. Simulation uses: an example of agent-based exercises for intentional contamination and recall decisions in food supply resilience planning. Related records: the H5N1 dairy study (case_study-us-h5n1-dairy-outbreak-economy-wide-cge) models another food supply shock with economy-wide effects.
